summary: A list of correct front-panel switch settings for IMPs and TIPs, written because wrong settings had caused problems. It covers the 516 IMPs and the 316 IMPs and TIPs, and says the RFC will be updated when settings change.

plainLanguage.summary: A checklist saying which switches on the network's machines must be up or down so they work right.

subtitle: Front-panel switch configuration for network routers

tldr.problem: Incorrect front-panel switch settings on IMPs and TIPs had caused network problems, and there was no documented checklist of correct settings.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC publishes a simple list of which switches must be ON or OFF for the two main IMP models (516 and 316) to operate correctly.
tldr.outcome: The checklist became standard operational guidance, to be kept at each site and used by field engineers during maintenance.

today: RFC 395 is classified as Unknown status. It was operational guidance for early ARPANET infrastructure, now of historical interest.

sections.title: Switch Configuration Problem
sections.content: Network sites had experienced problems because front-panel switches on IMPs (Interface Message Processors) and TIPs (Terminal Interface Processors) were set incorrectly. This RFC provides the correct settings as a checklist for site personnel and maintenance engineers to follow.
sections.plainLanguage: When switches are in the wrong position, the network machines stop working. This is the list of where every switch should be.

sections.title: 516 IMP Settings
sections.content: The model 516 IMP has a gray cabinet with two rows of indicator lights on the front panel. The correct settings are: Sense switches 1, 2, 3 and 4 set OFF; PFI/PFH set to PFI; HALT INH set OFF; W.D.T. (Watchdog Timer) set OFF; AUTO RSTRT set ON; and MEMORY PRTCT set OFF.
sections.plainLanguage: For the big gray machine, most switches go down, but the restart switch goes up.

sections.title: 316 IMP and TIP Settings
sections.content: The model 316 appears either as a TIP or in a black cabinet with one row of indicator lights. For this model, the only critical setting is Sense switches 1, 2, 3 and 4, all set to OFF (top half depressed). The RFC requests site personnel keep a copy nearby and advises field engineers to use it as a maintenance checklist.
sections.plainLanguage: For the smaller machine in the black box, just make sure the four sense switches are all pressed down.
